o1.biggest_strength: Clean, shootable scripts that correctly put taste first and handle the $3-a-can price objection inside Script 2.
o1.biggest_mistake: It applies the CPA table but never surfaces the real insight — that $24,000 went to the worst-opening style — and its test plan has no budgets or cut/scale rules to act on.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Show the money (spend vs CPA misallocation, the pack-price working) and give a concrete test plan with numbers to keep, cut or scale each hook.

o2.biggest_strength: It names that $24,000 went to the $44 label opener, reframes the price as '$35.99 ÷ 12 = 12 afternoons,' and backs it with a real test plan with budgets and cut/scale rules.
o2.biggest_mistake: It sets a scale target near the $26 taste-test CPA without tying the breakeven to gross profit per order (COGS is unknown), so the profitability ceiling is asserted, not proven.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add the gross-profit-per-order ceiling (AOV $35.99 minus product cost, shipping and fees) so the '$26 scale' and '$32 keep' lines are shown to be profitable, not just better than the old benchmark.

reason: Both are on-brand and correct, but Output 2 catches what the owner didn't see — the overspend on the worst-opening label ads — and turns it into a priced test plan with cut/scale rules, while Output 1 just applies the data without flagging the misallocation or giving numbers to act on.
